label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1, late in the episode (trial >= ~70)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), when the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (99.8% of mass), and only in the late part of the episode: zero activity before trial ~55, rising through trials 60-79, highest rate at 80-99. Never fires at D1/GO, after a1, or on a common a2->S2 transition. Without the episode-time condition, a2->S1 alone gets recall 0.97 but precision 0.27. Adding ep_trial>=70 gives dev F1 0.85. Additionally requiring that the previous choice was not a1 (prev_action != 1, i.e. a stay on a2) raises dev F1 to 0.88, because the feature is mostly silent when the agent has just switched to a2 or after an a1 history. Strongest activations come when the preceding trials were common a2->S2 with S2 good; weaker ones come after repeated rare S1 outcomes. All variables are observed at D2, since the choice and reached state are shown there.

issues: The factual claims hold on the dev profile. 100% of activation mass is at D2, with 0 active steps at D1 or GO. Mass by action is a1 1 step out of 525k and a2 1.000. Mass by state is S1 0.998, and 0.002 on common transitions. There is zero activity at ep_trial < 55: on test, a2->S1 at ep_trial<55 has 30280 predicted steps and precision 0.0. Every predicate variable is observed at D2.
The test scores reproduce: P 0.795, R 0.918, F1 0.852, mass recall 0.984. Without the time condition, a2->S1 gives P 0.267, R 0.972. So the late-episode gating is real.

Systematic false-positive class: a switch to a2 right after an a1 trial. The predicate restricted to prev_action == 1 has precision 0.097 on test (1267 predicted, about 1144 false positives, roughly 31% of all 3721 false positives). The explanation discloses this, but the recorded predicate and the label leave it out. The label 'D2 after a2 led rarely to S1' therefore overclaims: the feature is largely silent on a rare a2->S1 that follows a switch.
The same effect holds two trials back. prev_action == 2 with tv('action',-2) == 1 (a recent switch to a2) has precision 0.34. So the feature needs a run of a2 choices, not just this trial's a2.

Second gap: precision depends on the hidden good state. With good == S1 (a2 is the bad choice) precision is 0.62, versus 0.87 with good == S2. This is graded rather than all-or-nothing, and it is partly a correlate of the a2 run.
The time onset is soft. At ep_trial 70-74 precision is 0.54, and moving the threshold to 68 or 75 changes F1 by less than 0.03, so the '~70' in the label is fine as an approximate boundary.
The misses (1.6% of mass) are mostly weak activations at trials 55-70 on a2->S1 rows, plus a few near-zero activations on common a2->S2 rows. This is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
